sections.h2: What makes a fast house sale in Beaumont, TX different from other Texas cities?
sections.html:
Beaumont is a refinery and port city on the Neches River, and its housing market follows an industrial economy that has swung up and down for more than a century. Owners here often deal with older houses, mixed neighborhoods and a county tax system that runs through a separate appraisal district.

Census estimates put Beaumont at 112,967 people in mid-2025, down 1.8% from the April 2020 estimates base. Buyers have room to shop around, so a seller who arrives with a clear tax statement and a clean deed usually moves faster.

sections.h2: How did oil, rice and shipping shape Beaumont's neighborhoods?
sections.html:
The Handbook of Texas traces the city to a farm settled on the Neches in 1824 and describes a rice and lumber river port by the late 1800s. The Beaumont Rice Mill, founded in 1892, was the first commercial rice mill in Texas.

Then came Spindletop. After the 1901 gusher, the population rose from 9,427 in 1900 to 20,640 in 1910, and refineries and pipelines followed. Three oil companies that became Texaco, Gulf and Exxon formed in the first year of the boom, and a second Spindletop discovery in 1925 brought another burst of building. Houses from those waves still stand, so a Beaumont owner may be selling a property that predates modern code.

  • Seat of Jefferson County, 85 miles east of Houston along Interstate 10
  • One corner of the Golden Triangle with Port Arthur and Orange
  • Lamar University's main campus sits inside city limits
  • The city's two school districts merged in 1983

sections.h2: Which Beaumont landmarks and events appeal to buyers?
sections.html:
The same source lists more than thirty community and neighborhood parks, the Babe Didrikson Zaharias Museum, the McFaddin-Ward House, the Gladys City Boom Town Museum and the Texas Energy Museum. Yearly events include the South Texas State Fair and the Neches River Festival.

The Neches was channelized to Port Arthur in 1908 and deepened by 1916, and shipping and refining stayed central to the local payroll for decades. A seller can point to that employment base when describing the area, and buyers who work at the plants or the port often look at houses close to those jobs.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Beaumont housing?
sections.html:
For 2020-2024 the typical Beaumont owner-occupied home is valued at $166,400, and 55.3% of housing units are owner-occupied. Median gross rent stands at $1,121.

sections.h2: Who collects the tax on a Beaumont house, and when does it go late?
sections.html:
Three offices matter: the Jefferson Central Appraisal District values your house, each taxing unit picks its rate, and the Jefferson County Tax Assessor-Collector takes payment. The district itself says it levies, sets and collects nothing.

Texas values property as of January 1, and the lien for that year attaches the same day. Statements are mailed in October, and the Comptroller says you generally have until January 31 before February 1 delinquency begins. At that point the collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

  • Request a payoff statement from the tax office before signing a contract
  • Ask whether a prior-year balance sits on the account
  • Keep the receipt for the title company

sections.h2: Which homestead breaks matter to a Beaumont seller or buyer?
sections.html:
A buyer who moves in gets a school district exemption of $140,000, and a buyer who is 65 or disabled gets another $60,000 for school taxes, per the Comptroller. Cities and counties may adopt their own homestead exemptions too.

The Jefferson district's FAQ lists school districts, Jefferson County and the City of Port Arthur as the units that freeze tax for older and disabled owners. Anyone who missed the April 30 filing date can still apply for up to two years after the bill went delinquent, and the district charges nothing to file.

A separate cap holds a homestead's taxable value to a 10% yearly climb. For other real property worth $5,000,000 or less, the district says a 20% circuit breaker covers the 2024 through 2026 tax years and ends before 2027. New rooms or pools sit outside both caps.

sections.h2: What if a Beaumont appraisal looks too high?
sections.html:
Put the dispute in writing by whichever comes later: May 15, or the thirtieth day after the district mailed your notice. Jefferson notices for homes typically go out in mid-April, and an appraiser calls for an informal review ahead of any board hearing.

Losing at the Appraisal Review Board leaves two routes: a lawsuit in district court filed no later than 60 days after you receive the written decision, or binding arbitration, which the district says is open to every residential homestead no matter the value.

  • Bring sales of similar Beaumont houses from near January 1
  • Bring photos of foundation, plumbing or roof problems
  • Bring a survey if the district's measurements look off

sections.h2: How does foreclosure timing work for a Beaumont home?
sections.html:
Most Texas home loans carry a power of sale, so a lender can auction the house without a judge. Auctions happen on a first Tuesday, with bidding open from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m. at the place the commissioners court designates.

After a default notice the owner has 20 days to catch up and halt the process. The notice of sale must then land at least 21 days ahead of the auction, and the State Law Library notes a lender can still sue for a shortfall for two years. Ask the servicer for a payoff letter right away if you hope to sell first.

sections.h2: How do heirs sell an inherited Beaumont house?
sections.html:
When a will exists, it must go to probate within four years of the death, and a muniment of title can work if the only debts are liens on the property. With no will, a small estate affidavit covers estates worth $75,000 or less outside the homestead, but it does not fit other land.

An affidavit of heirship is sworn but not verified by a court, and no law forces a title insurer to accept it. A transfer on death deed skips probate if it was recorded before the owner died. Heirs who stay in the house can ask the appraisal district to extend the homestead exemption across the property by supplying the death certificate and an ownership affidavit.

sections.h2: Can a buyer run a Beaumont house as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Only with a city permit. Beaumont requires one for any stay shorter than 30 consecutive days, and the permit comes from Planning and Community Development and must be renewed yearly.

The permit number belongs on every online listing, and a hotel occupancy tax certificate is part of the package. Owners who advertise first may be fined, so a buyer with that plan should confirm the process before closing.

sections.h2: Where is the Beaumont deed filed after closing?
sections.html:
The Jefferson County Clerk keeps deed records for land inside the county, and a deed needs a signature plus an acknowledgment to be accepted.

The 2023 clerk manual lists a $5.00 fee for page one and $4.00 for every added page, plus records fees of up to $10 each for management and archives. The appraisal district changes ownership by looking at recorded deeds, which is why a mismatch on the tax roll usually points to a missing recording.

faqs.q: Does a Beaumont seller pay a state transfer tax?
faqs.a: The Comptroller and county clerk material describes recording fees on a deed and no deed transfer tax. Ask the Jefferson County Clerk for the exact fee schedule before you file.

faqs.q: What date do Beaumont taxes become late?
faqs.a: February 1 is the delinquency date for most bills. Statements arrive in October, and the Comptroller says payment is generally due by January 31.

faqs.q: Is a Beaumont homestead exemption still available if I forgot to file?
faqs.a: Probably. The Jefferson Central Appraisal District accepts a homestead application up to two years after the tax for that year turned delinquent.

faqs.q: Do Beaumont short-term rentals need permits?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a permit for stays under 30 consecutive days, a hotel occupancy tax certificate, and the permit number on each listing.

faqs.q: Who hears a protest of a Beaumont appraisal?
faqs.a: The Appraisal Review Board hears it after you file with the Jefferson Central Appraisal District. Your filing limit is the later of May 15 or 30 days after your notice was mailed.
